records.name: Akshat Mishra
records.resourcesWritten:
(1) NCERT books & JEE Mains previous year questions for Mathematics
(2) CAT material for VARC and DILR.

questions.general:
HR based:
(1) Introduce yourself Job based: What is your role (Cyber Security Analyst)?
(2) What is role of Cyber Security in today's world, one of the professors asked if the data on my phone is private to me anymore?
(3) What have you learnt from your experience? (4) Why PGDBA/ Business analytics? What do you expect from PGDBA, what are your future aspirations, any dream job?
I mentioned working as a consultant firm as my dream job. Follow up question was,
(5) How would PGDBA/ Business Analytics help in a consultancy firm?
(6) Do you think consultants will remain relevant in the future, can AI like ChatGPT pose a risk to their roles?
(7) Have you applied to other Business Analytics programs also? (I said yes and mentioned some names) Graduation Subjects:
(8) One weird question came up from a professor, when he asked me why I had taken a elective on Hazardous Waste Management, and there were few basic questions that followed on the subject. [I was not expecting a question on an elective that was totally unrelated to my graduation stream, but interviews are unpredictable]
(9) Another prof asked me if I know about need of consultants in Electrical Grid Management? (To this I answered No). So, she asked me to give it a thought as it was related to my profile.
(10) She also asked what are the challenges that can occur while managing a grid in recent times (I had no clue), so she gave me a hint about Renewable Energy sources being used and what possible challenges can they pose while managing the grid?
(11) What is Smart Metering?
questions.mathStats:
(1) They asked me if I had any course on Statistics/ Probability in my graduation, I didn't have any. They didn't believe me at first and crosschecked from my transcript.
(2) They asked one basic question on Random Variables, finding the Expectation, Variance and Standard deviation of the given data? [The twist was that they asked me to solve it on the black board, it felt that they wanted to check my confidence].
questions.gk: As I mentioned that I was a former state level Table Tennis player, they tried to get me involved in the recent controversy of the wrestlers' protest in Delhi, asked me why were they protesting and what are their demands?

records.tips:
(1) The difficulty level of Mathematics is increasing year by year, so you do need to practice difficult questions but do not waste time on JEE Adv level questions.
(2) For Interview prepare basic HR questions, questions on your profile/job experience and read newspaper for current affairs.
(3) If you have not studied Statistics or Probability in your graduation no need to take stress of that. (4) It would be better if you go with a genuine question prepared that you want to ask the interviewer at the last, instead of making a random question there. [After all last impression can add some brownie points].

questions.logical:
Chess puzzle:
Every square is numbered and number of each square is the average of all the squares surrounding it.
(1) Is it possible?
(2) Show an example.
(3) How to prove?
My answers:
(1) Yes its possible (I guessed)
(2) I asked permission to use pencil and paper. They started helping me out. Later sent to board with a marker where I assumed random numbers like 1 2 3 4 and started filling up the square but got stuck after a point. Finally they told me if all the numbers are 1 or 0 or any other number it could do.
(3) Then for the proof. I told we can take 64 variables and solve for 64 equations. They said its impractical to solve 64 eqs. I said its easily done in Python. They laughed and asked to leave as it was already 40 min + of interview time and they had to take for others.

records.tips: Interview is an ocean prepare whatever you say about yourself in CV and don't ignore current affairs and GK. No technical question was asked to me in the interview.

records.tips:
Interview is a lot about what panel you get and also your luck. Prioritize maximizing the written exam score so that you have a cushion and can afford to mess up a bit in the interview and still make it.
You need to have your +2 level math concepts rock-solid to ace the written exam, and as for VARC and DILR, some CAT type mocks might help since not a lot of content specifically geared towards PGDBA is available yet. DILR is generally very scoring so you should try to get all correct.
For interview, be absolutely confident with whatever work you do, and if you're a fresher, be confident in your undergrad or postgrad course subjects. Try having an idea about how you could incorporate analytics into your work field and why you wanna switch to analytics (if you are switching), and have a concrete understanding of the basics of linear algebra, probability and statistics. And of course, don't forget the general affairs!
